items.title: Journalism in the age of influencers | South Central @ 100
items.summary: A smartphone can record a protest, document police action and bring stories from the ground to thousands of people. But does that make the person behind the camera a journalist? And when an influencer describes themselves as an independent journalist, what should audiences expect from them? They are joined by Carl Lafrenais, Meghnad and Priyanshi Sharma of Peek TV for a conversation on journalism, credibility and the growing role of content creators in news. The conversation begins with Meghnad arguing that neither the government nor the Supreme Court should decide who qualifies as a journalist. For him, the people doing the work should be recognised as such. He points to those who are on the ground, recording events and preserving evidence. items.summary: त्योहारों का सीजन आते ही बाजारों में मिठाइयों की मांग तेजी से बढ़ जाती है. लेकिन मिठाइयों की बढ़ती मांग के साथ ही नकली और मिलावटी खाद्य पदार्थों का खतरा भी बढ़ने लगता है. खासकर दिल्ली-एनसीआर में, जहां देशभर से बड़ी मात्रा में खोया, पनीर और दूसरी खाद्य सामग्री पहुंचती है. ऐसे में सवाल है कि त्योहारों पर आप अपने घर जिस मिठाई को लेकर जा रहे हैं वह सेहत के लिए सुरक्षित भी है या नहीं? फूड सेफ्टी एंड स्टैंडर्ड्स अथॉरिटी ऑफ इंडिया (एफएसएसएआई) और दिल्ली फूड सेफ्टी डिपार्टमेंट की लगातार छापेमारी और कार्रवाई के बावजूद मिलावटी और अस्वच्छ खोया बड़ी मात्रा में पकड़ा जा रहा है. सिर्फ दिल्ली में ही इस त्योहारी सीजन में 3 नवंबर तक 10 हजार किलोग्राम से ज्यादा खोया नष्ट किया जा चुका है. इसके बावजूद मिलावट का सिलसिला थमने का नाम नहीं ले रहा है. आखिर त्योहारों पर बाजार में बिकने वाली मिठाइयां कितनी सुरक्षित हैं? मिलावट का यह कारोबार किस हद तक फैला हुआ है और खाद्य सुरक्षा विभाग की कार्रवाई का कितना असर हो रहा है? इन सवालों का जवाब जानने के लिए हमने गाजियाबाद, गौतम बुद्ध नगर और दिल्ली का दौरा किया. देखिए पूरी वीडियो रिपोर्ट- सत्ता बदली, हवा नहीं: प्रदूषण पर सरकार की पुरानी चाल, सिर्फ 3 बैठकों में निकाल दिया पूरा साल प्रदूषण पर प्रदर्शन, ‘हम सरकार से साफ हवा की भीख मांगने आए हैं’

items.summary: A Sessions Court in Kerala on Thursday refused to cancel the bail granted to the 17-year-old teenager accused of driving a Mercedes-Benz car and killing a scooterist. A Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) on October 26 granted the accused teenager bail. items.title: NCLT declares Videocon promoter Venugopal Dhoot bankrupt over ₹12,668 crore default
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) at Mumbai on Thursday declared former Videocon Industries promoter Venugopal Nandlal Dhoot bankrupt after admitting a petition filed by the State Bank of India (SBI) over outstanding dues of ₹12,668 crore. [SBI Vs Venugopal Dhoot] A Bench of Judicial Member Vinay Goel and Technical Member Charanjeet Singh Gulati passed the order under Section 126 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC). " We are satisfied that the Petition complies with all the requirements prescribed in Section 123 of the Code. Therefore, we consider it proper to admit this Petition ," the Tribunal said. The NCLT appointed Asish Narayan as the bankruptcy trustee and directed that Dhoot's estate vest in him immediately for administration and distribution among creditors. The proceedings arose from personal guarantees furnished by Dhoot for credit facilities extended to Videocon Industries and borrowings connected with Videocon Telecommunications Limited. SBI and its erstwhile associate banks had extended term loans and working capital facilities to the Videocon group. Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal announced the same via post on his X handle. The appointment has been made for a period of two years. The appointment follows the Supreme Court Collegium’s recommendation dated October 26 , which had approved the proposal for the appointment of Ajay Sharma and advocate Vaibhav Anant Sugdare as judges of the Bombay High Court. The Union government defended the cap, relying on an expert committee report that highlighted reduced caregiving capacities and health risks in advanced parental age. items.title: Goa SIR: Bombay High Court orders ECI to add back names of 6 voters deleted from electoral rolls
items.summary: In an order of significant political import, the Goa bench of the Bombay High Court on Thursday ordered the Election Commission of India (ECI) to add back names of six voters deleted from the voters' list during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the State. [Paresh Salgaonkar & Ors v. State of Goa & Ors.] After extensive hearings for four days, a division bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar pronounced the verdict on Thursday. "We have allowed petition. We have also rejected the prayer to keep this petition pending till Supreme Court decides (SIR's validity). We issue mandamus and direct the officer to include names of petitioners after confirming residence within 10 days," the Court said pronouncing its order. ECI counsel Gaurish Agni sought a stay on the order. However, the Court refused. "No stay. How can we grant stay on including names of voters in the list! You get a stay from Supreme Court," the bench said. Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. items.title: Challenge to delimitation: Calcutta High Court says no KMC elections based on redrawn wards for now
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Friday restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from calling elections to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) based on a delimitation notification issued in September that proposes to increase the number of civic wards from 144 to 209. A Division Bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Arjun Ray Mukherjee said that this restraining order will continue to operate until a petition challenging the validity of the delimitation exercise is decided. The order was passed on an appeal filed by Dipu Das, a former ward councillor under the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] regime between 2005 and 2010. " (Appeal filed by Das) is allowed in part, by modifying the impugned order (of single judge refusing to stay delimitation exercise) by restraining respondent no. 6, that is the West Bengal State Election Commission, from issuing a notification calling an election to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation on the basis of the amended Schedule II of the KMC Act... till disposal of WPA 31433 of 2026. items.title: India yet to liberate itself from English language even after 80 years of independence: Justice Gautam Chowdhary
items.summary: Allahabad High Court Justice Gautam Chowdhary on Monday said that India has not been able to liberate itself from the English language even after 80 years of independence from the British. Justice Chowdhary, who superannuates on November 8, made the comment in his retirement speech today. The speech was delivered in Hindi. "I want to underline that while we may have become free from the British constitutionally and geographically, nearly 80 years have passed, yet we have still not liberated ourselves from the English language. This is a matter every Indian must reflect upon: why, after 80 years, do we remain subservient to the language of those who ruled over us for 300 years?" the judge said. Justice Chowdhary added that his advocacy for Hindi may give the impression that he is opposed to other languages. However, he clarified that he harbours no animosity towards any language. "However, all these languages can be our maternal aunts (mausiyan); English can be our aunt from abroad. Let the aunts be accorded the utmost respect, I have no objection to that whatsoever. But seeing an Indian language, our own mother, being diminished inflicts deep pain and injury upon me," he added. Jus
